target_customer: Chinese consumers (voice assistant app and smart home speaker) and later OEM partners via Baidu
problem: Build an Alexa-like voice assistant and next generation operating layer for the Chinese market where Western assistants were not available.
business_model: Consumer app and hardware, later licensed platform inside Baidu
product_category: AI voice assistant and smart home hardware

founders.name: Cheng Lu
founders.background_notes: Name appears in sources as Lu Cheng, Lv Pin and Jesse Lyu. YC page gives no bio. After the acquisition he led Baidu smart home hardware and resigned in July 2018 per TechNode.

technical_complexity.rationale: Chinese language speech recognition, natural language understanding and hardware design for a small team in 2015.

defensibility.rationale: No evidence of data or distribution moat; large Chinese platforms had more data and users.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Baidu bought the company in February 2017 for an undisclosed sum, absorbing technology, product and about 60 staff.

market_need_then: Voice assistants were emerging globally (Alexa launched 2014) and press framed Raven as the Chinese answer to Alexa; direct evidence of demand at founding is thin.

identity.mascot_or_character: Voice assistant named Eva inside the Flow app

brand_strength.rationale: The branding search returned only other companies named Raven; press covered the acquisition, not the brand.

outcome_analysis: Raven Tech raised a reported 18 million dollars from DCM, ZhenFund, Matrix China, YC and Microsoft Accelerator, then was acquired by Baidu in February 2017 as Baidu built DuerOS. The product afterwards sold poorly, with fewer than 10,000 Raven H speakers made, a Baidu executive called the deal hasty, and the founder left in July 2018.
notes: Total funding about 18M (AVCJ, CB Insights 18.12M over 5 rounds) from DCM Ventures, ZhenFund, Matrix Partners China, MSA, YC and Microsoft Accelerator; per round amounts and dates were never disclosed in sources found, so no rounds are recorded. Seedtable lists a Series A of 18M in 2015-05, a single aggregator, unverified. Competitor search found no dated competitor sources near the batch, so the list is empty. Company website returned 503. The Microsoft accelerator timing differs between sources.
